sentences.text: Heard learned Counsel for the petitioner.
2. The petitioner is a Deputy Superintendent of Police (Dy.S.P.), presently serving in Baramati Taluka Police Station.

It appears that the respondent nos. 2 and 3 had filed a private complaint in the Court of the learned JMFC, Daund at Pune, being Criminal M.A. 1 of 3 14-4328-2022-WP=.doc No.109 of 2022, praying for an order under Section 156(3) order as against the petitioner.

sentences.text: 3. Pursuant to the said complaint, filed on 24.02.2022, the learned JMFC, vide order dated 29.09.2022 directed the police to register a complaint as against the petitioner for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 167, 218, 409, 420 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
4. Issue notice to the respondents, returnable on 2nd March, 2023.

Learned APP waives notice on behalf of the respondent no.1.
5.
In addition to Court notice, petitioner to serve the respondents by private notice and file an affidavit of service before the returnable date.

6. Learned Counsel for the petitioner to supply spare copies in the Registry, if not supplied, within two weeks from today, so as to enable the Registry to issue notice to the respondents, failing which,
petition
to stand
dismissed for non-prosecution, without further reference to the Court.

Having perused the papers and having heard learned Counsel for the petitioner, in the meantime,
till the next date, investigation to continue however, charge-sheet not to be filed.
Similarly, no coercive steps be taken against the petitioner, till the next date.

[PRITHVIRAJ K. CHAVAN, J.]
[REVATI MOHITE DERE, J.] 3 of 3
